blocks.content: The maximum strength of the council is fixed at one-third of the total strength of the assembly and the minimum strength is fixed at 40.

rows: Elected by members of local bodies like municipalities and district boards
Elected by MLAs from among persons who are not members of the assembly
Elected by graduates of 3 years' standing residing in the state
Elected by teachers of 3 years' standing in secondary or higher educational institutions
Nominated from fields of Literature, Science, Art, Cooperative Movement, and Social Service

items: Unlike Rajya Sabha nominations by the President, the Governor's nominations to the Legislative Council include 'Cooperative Movement' as an additional field.
1/3rd of members are elected by members of local authorities, and another 1/3rd are elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs).
Graduates and teachers elect 1/12th of the total members each, provided they meet the 3-year standing criteria.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The composition of the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is laid down under Article 171 of the Constitution of India.
The maximum strength of the council is one-third of the total strength of the state assembly, but minimum strength must be 40.
5/6th of the total members are indirectly elected, while 1/6th are nominated by the Governor.
Elections to the Legislative Council are held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
Governor nominates members possessing special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, cooperative movement, and social service.
